claim: Rhombus pricing: "Camera $399 (R120) to $3,299 (R600); license $149 per camera at the Professional tier"
problem: Misstated for the top-of-range SKU. On the same rhombus.com/pricing page, the R120/R200/R230/R410/R360S/R540/R545/R520/R150 all carry a $149 license, but the R600 multisensor camera is listed as $3,299 hardware + $649 license = $3,948 total (MSRP). So "license $149 per camera" is contradicted across the quoted $399-$3,299 range; a reader computes R600 at $3,448 instead of $3,948. Also, the page states "AI-features and cloud archiving not included in the Professional License," so the $748 R200 anchor is a video/cloud-storage price, not an AI-analytics price.
fix: Rewrite as: "Camera $399 (R120) to $3,299 (R600); license $149/camera (Professional tier) on all single-sensor SKUs, $649 on the R600; R600 total $3,948. Professional license excludes AI features and cloud archiving (Enterprise tier on request)." Keep the R200 $748 total, which is correct.

claim: NIJ LPR experiment: "LPR-equipped patrols scanned about eight times more plates than manual checking"
problem: The report's own executive summary says 8 to 10 times more plates checked, nearly 3x the hits and 2x the recoveries (combined across both phases). "About eight" sits at the floor of the reported range and understates the reported effect.
fix: Change to "8-10 times more plates checked, nearly 3 times the hits and twice the recoveries."

claim: "New Jersey landlords generally have no right to enter a rented dwelling without the tenant's consent or a court judgment" used to conclude an in-unit sensor program "needs lease language and tenant consent"
problem: The quoted sentence is verbatim from Truth in Renting, but the same document also states that "upon reasonable notification tenants must give the landlord and the landlord's employees access to the dwelling unit for the purpose of inspection and maintenance. Reasonable notification is normally one day" (N.J.A.C. 5:10-1.2). The brief omits that access right, which makes consent look like a harder blocker than the source supports for maintenance-type sensor installs.
fix: Add one clause: maintenance/inspection access must be granted on ~1 day's notice under N.J.A.C. 5:10-1.2, so lease language plus notice (rather than signed consent in every case) is the operative requirement; keep the separate consent rule for anything beyond inspection/maintenance.
